CORE-03.kft: SDT (top-down, theory-driven) and MI (bottom-up, practice-driven) are complementary developmental pathways; systematic integration is possible and desirable. The integration hinge: MI researchers might want to embrace autonomy/volition as the fundamental basic process underlying therapeutic change (SDT-framed proposal - authored from the SDT side, not a neutral synthesis); autonomy-supportive communication is the practical grammar connecting the two.
CORE-03.ess: not_quantifiable - conceptual/theoretical integration paper (argues, does not measure; no data in source).
CORE-03.lim: The integration is a proposal, not a tested intervention; the proposal is SDT-framed advocacy (lead author is an SDT researcher; the hinge is asymmetric - MI is asked to embrace autonomy); SDT's universality claims vs MI's pragmatic roots remain a live tension (batch-1 fault line 5); no new data.
CORE-03.di: If MI's efficacy were shown to operate through mechanisms other than autonomy/volition (e.g., alliance, expectancy), the integration hinge weakens; if SDT's autonomy construct does not map cleanly onto MI's spirit, the proposed synthesis is decorative.
CORE-03.h1: yes - autonomy support improves sustained motivation and behavior change; NOTE: asserted by this source's theory, demonstrated in sibling-row evidence (CORE-05 meta-analysis) - cross-row-supported, not source-demonstrated.
CORE-03.h2: partial - volition as a vector (quality of motivation), not compliance-as-output.
CORE-03.dimpl: The tool's register supports the person's own volitional process (choice, rationale, acknowledgment of resistance) - never a tool-owned motivational layer; volitional outcomes are the person's, not engagement metrics. M2 need-support profile stays a design heuristic, not a validated manipulation (batch-1 pilot rule). Telos remains the person's own (CORE-02 ruling carries).
CORE-03.cimpl: Volition over compliance - the tool must never purchase behavior through compliance-shaped grammar; the person's own volitional process is the criterion (autonomy support is the means, not a lever), and coercion-by-nudge is a false integration (Tier-P application under A1-01/HUI-2024 criterion).

CORE-11.kft: The beneficial effects of goal setting are overstated; specific, challenging goals produce systematic side effects: narrow focus that neglects non-goal areas, rise in unethical behavior, distorted risk preferences, corrosion of organizational culture, reduced intrinsic motivation. Goal setting should be treated as prescription-strength medication: careful dosing, side-effect monitoring, close supervision, warning label (10-question caution list: goal specificity/comprehensiveness, challenge and failure costs, goal authorship, time horizon, risk appetite, unethical-behavior safeguards, idiosyncratic tailoring, culture/cooperation, intrinsic motivation, performance-vs-learning goals).
CORE-11.ess: not_quantifiable - narrative/argumentative review with case evidence (Sears, Enron-era); no pooled ES; the replicated positive linear difficulty-performance relation (Locke & Latham) is acknowledged as a qualitative quote only, not re-quantified.
CORE-11.lim: Position/argumentative review (HBS Working Paper 09-083, unrefereed draft - charted text is the working-paper version; version of record = Acad Mgmt Perspect 23(1):6-16); selective emblematic cases; side-effect magnitudes not estimated; boundary conditions are the authors' own untested prescriptions; advocacy-adjacent in the OPPOSITE direction from CORE-10's originator-authored advocacy - the two rows draw on the SAME underlying experimental corpus and are opposing advocacy poles, NOT mutually confirming (never sum them).
CORE-11.di: If goal setting's benefits hold without the named side effects under ordinary conditions (moderate goals, no reward link, user-set), the 'over-prescribed' verdict is overstated; the article itself concedes the positive linear relation under boundary conditions (commitment, ability, no conflicting goals).
CORE-11.h1: partial - specific challenging goals boost performance (replicated, acknowledged by the source); the row's warning concerns side effects.
CORE-11.h2: yes - goal architecture is a vector (goal type, authorship, time horizon, risk articulation, culture/cooperation), not a scalar difficulty dial.
CORE-11.dimpl: Goal failure modes -> guardrails on the goal grammar (M4a): the tool's goal-setting layer must carry the warning-label logic - performance vs learning goals, user-set goals, time-horizon checks, risk articulation, intrinsic-motivation assessment, cooperation-aware goal units (Design Veto Catalogue, CF-1). Pairs with CORE-10's goal-grammar row as the opposing pole of a held tension.
CORE-11.cimpl: Goal narrowing as moral flattening - a goal scalar (output) that blinds the person to non-goal areas reproduces the Sears pattern (unethical shortcutting under goal pressure); S7 moral-hollowing guard (Tier-P).

CORE-12.kft: ABSTRACT-LEVEL CHARTING (documented decision 2026-08-13): the 741-page ONR-funded monograph (Harvard, 1949-1955) is the empirical foundation of schedule-controlled behavior - systematic mapping of how fixed/variable interval and ratio schedules and extinction control operant responding. The textbook summary (variable-ratio schedules are most extinction-resistant) is the standard reading of the book's findings but was NOT verified against text this pass (lending-only) - Tier-P, unverified.
CORE-12.ess: not_quantifiable - no numeric extraction at abstract level; no schedule parameter may be quantified from this row.
CORE-12.lim: Full text unread (archive lending only); animal subjects (pigeons/rats), 1957 methods; era-bound evidence base - the monograph predates matching-law and later schedule research, so catalog-level claims cannot distinguish findings that survived replication from those later qualified; claims stay at catalog/documentary level (Tier-P).
CORE-12.di: CORE-13's review (read this pass) shows schedule control is more complex than a single 'VR most extinction-resistant' rule: fixed-interval scallop depends on absolute interval duration (timescale-invariance violations), matching is overdetermined, chain schedules can collapse. Any tool rule importing one schedule heuristic would overreach.
CORE-12.h1: yes - contingency/schedule design shapes behavior (mechanism direction, Tier-P).
CORE-12.dimpl: Contingency/schedule design (M4c) - schedule dynamics (extinction, satiation, contrast) are veto criteria for any tool-side reinforcement layer: the tool must not possess one; where schedule concepts inform the design grammar, import direction + bounded band only, never a point rule.
CORE-12.cimpl: Any contingency-scheduled reward architecture in a tool is veto territory (CF-3): schedule control of the person is the dependency/captive-self failure mode per the CORE-16 criterion ('the self becomes captive of a certain kind of order'). The specific variable-ratio mechanism remains an UNVERIFIED hypothesis (abstract-level row), not a charted finding.
CORE-12.cs: causal (lab-bounded, animal; catalog-attributed - unverified against text, Tier-P)

CORE-13.kft: Operant behavior is behavior 'controlled' by its consequences (source terms); the review documents lawful but complex schedule effects across interval timing (proportional timing, Weber's law, linear waiting) and choice (matching law and its extensions, concurrent chains, self-control). Design discipline (matrix synthesis vocabulary - 'consequence-engineering' is the matrix's gloss, not the source's term): consequence design is not simple - matching is highly overdetermined (reveals little about underlying dynamics), molar response rate misses the fixed-interval scallop, multi-link chains can extinguish early links, and (per the authors) no integrated theory of conditioned reinforcement exists (contested within-field position, attributed).
CORE-13.ess: not_quantifiable - narrative review; functional relations (matching, scalar property) described qualitatively; no pooled ES, no external d-value imports.
CORE-13.lim: Animal-primary review with brief human coverage (human schedule results 'broadly similar' but with weaker reinforcers - verified); Annual Review solicited chapter, non-systematic; senior author is a committed behaviorist whose own theories (linear waiting, tuned-trace) are foregrounded - advocacy-adjacent within-field; literature to ~2001 (author manuscript); 'no integrated theory of conditioned reinforcement' is the authors' contested position, not settled fact.
CORE-13.di: Timescale invariance is only approximately true (fixed-interval curvature depends on absolute interval length); matching maximization fails on simple RID schedules; chain responding can extinguish - schedule control has documented failure modes that naive contingency design would miss.
CORE-13.h1: yes - schedules/contingencies control behavior (mechanism direction, Tier-P; the review synthesizes causal experiments but is itself a review - citation-is-not-evidence).
CORE-13.dimpl: Temper naive contingency design - the tool must not import simple reward/punish rules as calibrated scalars; consequences are powerful but non-obvious in their dynamics; use direction + bounded band; watch extinction/satiation dynamics (Motivation Crowding Watch Card, CF-3).
CORE-13.cimpl: Consequence engineering has hidden costs - a behaviorist reward grammar applied to the person is the manipulation paradigm (HUI-2024 cybernetics guard; consistent with batch-2 CORE-09 refusal: the loop must not treat the person as the plant). Consequences as mirror, not leash: the tool surfaces consequences as information for the person's judgment, with no contingent scheduling or withholding on the tool side - the mirror is disclosure, not a loop; any contingency pairing is person-authored (Tier-P).

CORE-14.kft: Cognition is partly constituted by body, tools, and environment (active externalism). Parity principle: if a part of the world functions as a process which, were it done in the head, we would have no hesitation in recognizing as part of the cognitive process, then that part of the world is part of the cognitive process ('cognitive processes ain't (all) in the head'). Otto's notebook plays the role of memory - the extended mind; the extended self follows; interfering with someone's environment can have the same moral significance as interfering with their person.
CORE-14.ess: not_quantifiable - philosophical argument (thought experiments, parity intuitions).
CORE-14.lim: Philosophical thesis, not empirical result; contested (internalist critiques; belief-criteria conditions - trust, constancy, endorsement - delimit the claim); no experimental test; the parity principle licenses framing but predicts no user effect - any empirical claim must come from other rows (CORE-17/19/20), not from this source.
CORE-14.di: If the notebook fails the belief criteria (untrusted, rarely consulted, not endorsed), it is not part of belief - the authors set these conditions themselves; empirical findings that cognitive offloading does not yield the predicted effects would weaken the constitutive (not merely causal) claim.
CORE-14.h1: partial - the source's thesis is CONSTITUTIVE (environment constitutes cognition under parity criteria, active externalism), not a weaker causal 'shapes' claim; causal-effect claims must come from empirical rows.
CORE-14.h2: yes - cognitive design is world-design (vector: ecology, technology, locality, reversibility).
CORE-14.dimpl: Warrant for treating environment design as cognitive design - the tool's capture architecture, external memory, and ambient structure ARE part of the user's cognitive system (Digital Capture Architecture); but the environment is the user's locality: the tool must remain a revision-capable prosthesis, not a replacement (S10; HUI-2024 prosthesis-vs-replacement gate).
CORE-14.cimpl: Cognitive design is also world-design - externalization is not neutral; designing the cognitive environment is designing the person's world (organology per HUI-2024 - exteriorized memory is an organ of the person; locality per A1-01's human-milieu cosmotechnics); extended mind licenses locality, not colonization, and locality means the person retains authorship and revision authority over a SHARED environment - not exclusion, which would forfeit prosthesis (criterion-derived Tier-P application under the C&C parity criterion, not Hui's finding).

CORE-16.kft: Optimal experience (flow) occurs when attention is ordered: information congruent with goals -> psychic energy flows effortlessly (the opposite of psychic entropy). The felt record, in capture order: deep absorption (action and awareness merge; the activity becomes spontaneous, almost automatic); the worries and frustrations of everyday life drop out of awareness; a sense of control; time distortion (hours pass in minutes); loss of self-consciousness, yet the self paradoxically emerges stronger afterward and can reach self-transcendence; clear goals and immediate feedback; challenges matched to skills (the 'golden ratio' is qualitative metaphor - no numeric ratio exists in the source); and the autotelic quality - the experience is an end in itself, done for the doing. Flow builds a more complex self; the conditions are suppliable, the state is not forceable ('Control over consciousness cannot be institutionalized'); flow activities can become addictive - 'the self becomes captive of a certain kind of order, and is then unwilling to cope with the ambiguities of life', losing 'the freedom to determine the content of consciousness'.
CORE-16.ess: not_quantifiable - theoretical synthesis grounded in the author's ESM corpus; zero statistics in the source text; the 'golden ratio' must never be operationalized as a numeric challenge-skill ratio.
CORE-16.lim: Theoretical + descriptive (ESM/experience-sampling, self-report retrospective base; signal-contingent sampling and self-report reactivity are known ESM limits); originator-authored synthesis drawing on the author's own corpus (self-study reliance - literature-overlap/double-counting risk with any flow evidence row, same rule as CORE-10/CORE-11); individual differences (autotelic personality); the addiction passage is the phenomenon's shadow side (dependency, escapism, narrowed attention), not a calibrated risk.
CORE-16.di: If challenge-skill balance is neither necessary nor sufficient (flow reported in low-challenge or feedback-free contexts), the conditions claim is incomplete; the addiction passage shows flow can capture rather than liberate - a tool that manufactures flow-like reward states reproduces the captive-self failure mode and deletes the freedom-to-return.
CORE-16.h1: yes - flow is an achievable optimal-experience state (as the theory asserts; demonstration rests on the author's own corpus).
CORE-16.h2: partial - flow as attunement (vector), never extraction (scalar output).
CORE-16.dimpl: Conditions suppliable; state not forceable - the tool can supply flow's conditions (clear goals, immediate feedback, challenge options at the person's choosing) but must not command or extract the state; 'Control over consciousness cannot be institutionalized' (p. 21): a reliably reproduced condition-set is, by the book's own logic, no longer flow; challenge calibration is person-side, never tool-side (A9-06 person-designated principle carries); flow is respite-with-return - the tool must preserve the freedom to leave flow and return to ambiguity, never optimize flow-time (flow conditions are structural/presence-based 0/1, never calibrated scalars).
CORE-16.cimpl: Flow as attunement, not extraction - flow is the image of harmonious absorption; the tool cultivates the person's own ordering of attention; the addiction passage (captive self, loss of the freedom to determine the content of consciousness) is the anti-veneer test: a tool manufacturing dependency on flow-like rewards fails the criterion.

CORE-17.kft: ABSTRACT-LEVEL CHARTING (documented decision 2026-08-13): the 1982 Oxford UP volume is the canonical methods text for SCEDs - multiple-baseline and related designs control history/maturation without a control person, licensing within-case causal inference. Corroborated at abstract level by Kazdin 2021 (JEAB 115(1):56-85, paywalled body): core features of SCEDs, how key/ancillary features evolved, special strengths, and challenges impeding integration remain live.
CORE-17.lim: Abstract-level charting (full texts gated: 1982 book lending-only, 2021 JEAB paywalled); 1982 1st ed. vs later editions differ (Google Books landing is a later edition); SCED inference is per-case (no population generalization); visual-analysis-vs-statistical-power debate is live (Kazdin 2021 abstract); concrete SCED practice conventions (phase lengths, baseline counts) are NOT in the charted base - the pilot's phase plan must be validated against a readable methods text before execution.
CORE-17.di: SCED causal claims are contested (the 'challenges' Kazdin names); without a no-reward baseline phase, no causal inference (batch-1/2 rule; DKR 1999 excluded no-control studies); N-of-1 evidence cannot license population claims.
CORE-17.h1: partial - SCED is the Tier-C pilot's inference spine (design-licenses claim, Tier-P).
CORE-17.dimpl: Spine of the Tier-C pilot (SCED): phase logic = baseline -> intervention -> follow-up; multiple-baseline across behaviors needs >=2 staggered baselines; visual-analysis rule pre-specified in the Preregistration Packet; reporting per SCRIBE (CORE-18); claims bounded to the individual (Tier-P).
CORE-17.cimpl: Per-case claims stay per-case - the pilot never trades the person's singular record for a population average (Tier-P: an inference-scope application, not a moral valuation of uniqueness); rigorous N-of-1 inference is the guard against false generalization.
CORE-17.cs: conceptual (methods source - prescribes inference, demonstrates none); within-case causal inference is licensed only for executed SCEDs that include a baseline phase; no population generalization

CORE-18.kft: SCRIBE 2016 = a 26-item checklist for reporting single-case research, developed through 2 Delphi surveys + a 2-day expert consensus meeting (CONSORT-family process), published simultaneously in 9 journals; purpose: clear, complete, accurate reporting (title/abstract through results/discussion); explicitly NOT design/analysis guidance.
CORE-18.lim: Reporting standards do not guarantee design validity ('the SCRIBE 2016 does not make recommendations about how to design, conduct or analyze data from single-case experiments' - verbatim); consensus/Delphi-based (expert judgment, not empirical test); checklist burden; SCRIBE's 26 items assume single-case phase designs - fit with MRT-style component reports (CORE-19) is not automatic.
CORE-18.di: A fully SCRIBE-compliant report of a poorly designed SCED is still poor evidence - reporting quality does not equal evidence quality (the reporting-guideline version of citation-is-not-evidence).
CORE-18.h1: partial - the pilot's reporting follows SCRIBE (reporting quality is a necessary but not sufficient condition of pilot validity).
CORE-18.dimpl: Governs SCED reporting quality - the pilot's Preregistration Packet and final report must address the 26 items, with an explicit reporting-mapping step for MRT-style component reports (CORE-19); the quality rubric must separate reporting score from design validity.
CORE-18.cimpl: Transparency as anti-self-deception - reporting discipline makes the tool's own claims auditable (the person can see the record; reversibility S10).

CORE-19.kft: MRT = experimental design for optimizing JITAIs: participants are microrandomized at decision points to intervention components; enables causal modeling of proximal effects of individual components and time-varying effect moderation (when and for whom components work); overcomes RCT limitations (whole-package evaluation) and factorial-design limitations for adaptive interventions.
CORE-19.ess: not_quantifiable - methods paper; HeartSteps is an illustrative example only (no MRT effect estimates exist in the paper).
CORE-19.lim: Methods overview, no primary results; causal claims are proximal, not distal; requires sensing/delivery infrastructure - MRT estimation needs many microrandomized decision points per participant (decision-point density/power feasibility is unexamined for the pilot); assumptions to be pre-registered: no carryover/no-engagement effects, no interference between participants (SUTVA), correct time-varying model specification - violation biases estimates; component optimization does not equal whole-ecology validation.
CORE-19.di: If component effects are not time-varying or carryover/engagement effects violate MRT assumptions, estimates are biased; MRT optimizes components - a separate confirming phase (CORE-20) is still required for the full system.
CORE-19.h1: partial - the pilot's component testing uses MRT logic (design-licenses claim: executed microrandomization licenses causal attribution of proximal effects only).
CORE-19.dimpl: For JITAI-style component testing - used only where the person opts into prompt density; prompt frequency is person-capped, never a tool-tuned scalar. The tool's component testing (Digital Capture Architecture) uses microrandomization for proximal-effect attribution; full-system claims require a confirming phase (CORE-20); decision points must be defined in the capture architecture.
CORE-19.cimpl: Rigor for the digital channel - honest causal attribution of digital components serves the person; but component optimization must never treat the person's attention or engagement as an optimizable resource (S1/S10 guard; the tool stays a locality, not an optimizer of the user).

CORE-20.kft: MOST = three-phase strategy for building/evaluating behavioral interventions: screening (efficiently identify active components), refining (fine-tune components/dosage), confirming (standard randomized confirmatory trial of the optimized package); SMART = design for building adaptive interventions (identify tailoring variables and decision rules empirically). Both use randomized experimentation for valid inference - an alternative to the slow RCT -> post-hoc -> revision cycle.
CORE-20.ess: not_quantifiable - methods overview; the illustration is explicitly hypothetical ('based on, but not identical to or an account of, the work of one of the authors') - no component result exists to chart.
CORE-20.lim: Methods overview; methods were 'relatively untried at this writing' (2007) - treat MOST logic as heuristic scaffold with built-in fallbacks, not validated machinery; component-by-component optimization can miss non-additive interactions; confirming phase still requires a full RCT; screening 'may be made on the basis of estimated effect size' - a design detail that invites exactly the external-ES import the matrix forbids (flagged for the pilot's component-screening protocol); component-level optimization does not equal ecology-level efficacy.
CORE-20.di: If component effects interact non-additively beyond what factorial screening captures, the optimized package underperforms; MOST optimizes components - the tool must not mistake component optimization for ecosystem cultivation.
CORE-20.h1: partial - the pilot's Intervention Component Library follows MOST (design-licenses claim: ONLY the MOST confirming phase - a standard RCT of the optimized package - licenses package-level causal claims, and the Tier-C pilot is not a confirming-phase trial).
CORE-20.dimpl: Channel attribution once components defined - the pilot's component library + attribution logic follows MOST's screening -> refining -> confirming sequence (directly feeds the Tier-C pilot); optimization results must never be labeled efficacy; the pilot is screening/refining-stage logic.
CORE-20.cimpl: Avoid confounding the whole ecology - the tool must not optimize the person's total environment as if it were a component set; the ecology is the person's locality, not the optimizer's. The operative distinction is standpoint: the person may optimize their own locality; the tool may not (S1; matrix locality guard anchored in A1-01's human-milieu cosmotechnics and HUI-2024's technodiversity/organology - matrix vocabulary, not a Hui-2024 phrase).
